fields.h1: Build a Contract Approval Workflow That Reads the Terms
fields.hero_description: Get a contract approval workflow that reads each contract's value and terms and brings in the approvers they call for.
fields.features_heading: What Decides Who Signs Off on a Contract
fields.features_subheading: Your contract policy, built as an app by Emergent: which terms bring in which approver, when reminders go out, and who decided.
fields.feature_1:
Routing rules written as sentences

Describe each rule as you would to a new sales rep: changed payment terms add the controller. From that description, Emergent builds the request form and the routing behind it.
fields.feature_2:
Key terms read from the draft

The app reads the terms your rules use from each uploaded draft, such as payment terms and total value. A term it reads with low confidence goes to a person to confirm first.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders before a contract stalls

An approver who has not decided in the time you set gets a reminder in Slack or by email. If the contract still waits after that, it escalates to the backup you name for them.
fields.feature_4:
One record of every decision

Each decision and its comment is saved with the contract version it covers, in a database you own. Who agreed to net 60 is answered on the contract record, not in an inbox.
fields.feature_5:
Starts where the deal already lives

The app connects to any tool with an API. A contract request can open from a HubSpot deal, and the approval status syncs back to that deal, where the rep already works.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to GitHub

On paid plans, the full code of the app exports to your GitHub repository. Anyone you trust can read the routing logic line by line there and keep their own copy of it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Net 60 pulls the controller into the deal

Orvane Freight returns its $96,000 order form with payment terms changed to net 60. The app reads the term from the redline and finds it differs from your standard net 30. The controller, Ilse Vantongeren, joins as an approver, and the rep, Tobiah Rensselaer, waits for her.
fields.tab_content_2:
A $54,000 yearly value waits on the CFO

Harrowgate Data quotes three years at once: $162,000 in total, or $54,000 a year. Your rule adds the CFO when annual value passes $50,000. The app divides the total by the term before it routes. Priyanka Szabo, the department head, has approved. The contract now waits for Leon Achebe, the CFO.
fields.tab_content_3:
Renewal goes to its owner 30 days ahead of notice

Sendara Cloud renews on its own on March 31, 2027, at $24,000 a year, unless you cancel with 60 days' notice. That puts the notice deadline on January 30, 2027. On December 31, 2026, 30 days before it, the app sends the owner, Fenwick Oduya, a direct message asking him to approve the renewal or cancel it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Your NDA skips review, theirs goes to counsel

Two NDAs arrive in the same week, and the request form asks whose paper each one is on. Quillon Robotics accepts your NDA template with no edits, and the app approves it with no reviewer. Marlowe Biotech sends its own NDA instead, and the app routes it to your counsel, Ada Iheanacho, before anyone signs.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Contract Approval Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a contract approval workflow that routes each contract by its terms and value, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the terms that change the route
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull last year's signed contracts and sort them by type, such as vendor agreements and NDAs. Note who approved each one and how many days it waited, and mark any contract that someone signed before every approver had decided.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the terms that should bring in another approver, such as payment terms or a liability cap. Keep the list short, because every term on it is one more field each request has to carry.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each trigger as a number or a fact, not a judgment call: an annual value over $50,000 adds the CFO. A rule with a number in it runs the same way for every rep.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the contracts that need no reviewer at all, such as an NDA on your own template with no edits. Routine paper that clears on its own leaves counsel more time for the contracts that need a careful read.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide how long a contract may sit with one person before a reminder goes out, and who takes over after that. Name a backup for every approver, including the CFO.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the rules in plain English, one sentence each, and give them to Emergent. It builds the app that runs them, and it changes any rule when you prompt again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run five signed contracts from last quarter through the rules before going live. Check that each one reaches the approvers it reached in real life, and fix any rule that sends it somewhere else.

faq_plan.q: What is a contract approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: A contract approval workflow is the set of rules a contract passes through before anyone signs it: who reviews it and which terms bring in an extra approver. Contract approval itself is the process of submitting, reviewing, assessing, and approving whole contracts or specific terms. The workflow turns that process into rules that run the same way on every contract.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a contract approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: Write down which contract terms should change who approves, then describe those rules to Emergent's AI automation builder in plain English. It builds the app that routes each contract and logs every decision. Run a handful of last quarter's contracts through it before your team starts sending new ones.

faq_plan.q: How do I track a contract approval workflow across multiple departments?
faq_plan.hint: How do i track contract approval workflows across multiple departments?
faq_plan.a: Give every contract one record that shows each department's decision and how long the contract has waited with it. A board filtered by department then lets each team see its own queue without chasing the others. The app Emergent builds can show that board as a live dashboard, sorted by days waiting.

faq_plan.q: Should a contract approval workflow check vendor invoices against the signed contract?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you pay vendors under the contracts you approve. Store the agreed price and end date on the contract record, and have your invoice approval workflow compare each invoice with them before payment. An invoice dated after the end date, or billed at a higher price, then goes to the contract owner.

faq_plan.q: How should a contract approval workflow handle a contract redlined after approval?
faq_plan.a: Send it back through approval, but only to the approvers whose terms the redline touched. Compare the new version with the approved one: a corrected notice address can be logged without rerouting, while a change to payment terms goes back to finance. Keep each approval tied to the version it covered.

faq_plan.q: Who belongs in a contract approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: Name one approver per kind of risk, not one per department. A split that works for many teams: the department head approves the spend, finance approves value and payment terms, and counsel approves any change to your standard legal terms. Add an approver only when a rule says what they are checking.

faq_plan.q: How is a contract approval workflow different from approving marketing content?
faq_plan.a: The triggers differ. A contract routes on money and terms, such as value and payment terms, while a marketing piece routes on the words themselves: brand voice and any claims counsel should see. If your team reviews both, keep them as separate flows and use a content approval workflow for posts and ads.

faq_plan.q: What fields does a contract approval workflow need on the request form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for what your routing rules read: counterparty, contract type, total value, term length, payment terms, renewal date, notice period, and whose paper it is on. Add the contract owner, the person every reminder should reach. The form comes from the same prompt as the rules, and Emergent changes both when you prompt again.

faq_plan.q: How many approvers should a contract approval workflow have?
faq_plan.a: As few as each contract's risk calls for: none for an unedited NDA on your own template, more only when a rule names a reason. Each approver you add is one more person the contract waits on. Count the approvers on last year's contracts and drop any whose review never changed a decision. The apps Emergent builds have no per-approver seats.

faq_plan.q: Should sales and vendor contracts share one contract approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: Yes: one approval workflow can carry both, as long as each contract type has its own rules. A sales contract puts discounts and payment terms in front of finance, because they change what you collect. A vendor contract puts spend and renewal terms first, because they change what you pay. Both can share the same reminders and decision record.
